title: Universal curve-test datum for a failure
statement:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all
$q'\leq q-1$, but $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. Then there exist a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X & \longleftarrow & X' & \longleftarrow & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow h\\
S & \longleftarrow & S' & \longleftarrow & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

with both squares Cartesian, where

1. $S'$ is affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed
function field;
1. $K$ is algebraically closed and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ is
dominant (in other words $K$ is an extension of the function
field of $S'$),

and there exists an integer $d\mid n$ such that
$R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)$ is nonzero.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.7, [Tag `0F08`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F08).*)

proof.text: Choose the field failure using [sbc-lem-bc-failure-field] and pass to its algebraic closure using [sbc-lem-bc-integral-surjective]. Normalize the affine base in that algebraic closure using Etale.exists_normalization_of_isAlgClosed, and transport the failure to this integral base change using [sbc-lem-bc-integral-base]. This is the unchanged geometric part of Etale.exists_isPullback_not_isZero_higherDirectImage.

By [sbc-lem-bc-injectivity], in the unchanged existing proof the normalized base-change map is mono and is not an isomorphism, so its target is nonzero. For the coefficient step apply [lem-sbc-prime-cyclic-detection] to obtain a prime $r\mid n$, not a unit in $\Lambda$, with nonzero prime-cyclic higher direct image. If the image on $\Lambda/(r)$ were zero, [lem-sbc-prime-quotient-detection] would make that prime-cyclic image zero. This contradiction proves the existing coefficient theorem with $d=r$. Finally assemble the datum as in the existing proof; all geometry and divisibility witnesses are unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Existing geometric reduction retained; coefficient reduction through prime cyclic detection and the ring-quotient retract
